title: Auditions and the metronome test
summary: Auditions were common, such as the Three Deuces in Chicago and New Orleans, where a captain used a metronome.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well you can't even get them to audition. Right, right, right. Which reminds me, did you ever make many auditions?

Oh man, that was a common thing, auditions. I tell the band, listen man, we've got an audition tomorrow. Just like the Three Deuces, we went down and played the Three Deuces in Chicago where Tatum was playing and we must have played a half day for the boss man. We auditioned here in New Orleans to play on the boat. And Captain Vern Stryfus came to hear us up at the Pelican. He used to bring the metronome with him to see if your tempos varied. He was tough. Sure they did this on the boat. If any of these guys can remember, they watched the metronome to see if the bands varied.
